WHAT RUNS BY ITSELF

Two Windows scheduled tasks run this tree every day with nobody at the keyboard. Their state below is schtasks /Query /TN <name> /FO LIST /V, read at generation; the register line is the one the tool that registered the task prints.

BrainLadder (daily 04:00)

  • registered: NO (schtasks exited -1: spawnSync schtasks ENOENT); register it with the line below
  • newest log: none under bench/verdicts/ladder

Register, remove, query (the tool prints each schtasks line before it runs it):

node tools/schedule-ladder.mjs --register
node tools/schedule-ladder.mjs --remove
node tools/schedule-ladder.mjs --status
schtasks /create /tn BrainLadder /tr "cmd /c cd /d /home/user/brain && node bench/ladder.mjs --log" /sc daily /st 04:00 /f

BrainAutopilot (daily 05:00)

  • registered: NO (schtasks exited -1: spawnSync schtasks ENOENT); register it with the line below
  • newest log: none under bench/verdicts/autopilot

Register, remove, query (the tool prints each schtasks line before it runs it):

node tools/schedule-autopilot.mjs --register
node tools/schedule-autopilot.mjs --remove
node tools/schedule-autopilot.mjs --status

The registered command matches the tool's own line: BrainLadder not registered, BrainAutopilot not registered. The autopilot task runs a guarded tick that then runs exactly this (tools/schedule-autopilot.mjs tickArgv), its transcript appended to bench/verdicts/autopilot/<date>.log:

node tools/budget.mjs --ram-mb 6000 --disk-mb 2000 --dir state/self -- node --max-old-space-size=6000 bin/brain.mjs self-code --auto --soak 90 --author on --json

HOW TO CHECK

node daemon/health.mjs --gaps
node daemon/health.mjs
node bench/ladder.mjs
node tools/schedule-autopilot.mjs --status
node tools/schedule-ladder.mjs --status
node bin/brain.mjs self-code --auto --dry --json

node daemon/health.mjs --gaps prints the gap counters in one line with no server; with no flag it serves GET /health on 127.0.0.1:8080 (HEALTH_PORT overrides). node bench/ladder.mjs with no flag prints the board from the verdicts on disk. The dry self-code run lists every candidate the loop would try, writes nothing and asks no model.

  • its last decision: resumed, key resume:public-gsm8k:1, at 2026-09-26T12:54:20.898Z
  • newest gap ledger: state/self/gaps.jsonl, 245 gaps (0 unparseable lines), 87 with a trial, written 2026-09-26T20:50:29.718Z; by kind: board item 71, bar never completed 7, missed 18, unreadable bar 10, ladder 6, gate red 1, gate slow 11, open 121
node self/gaps.mjs

node self/gaps.mjs rebuilds the ledger from the verdicts, the gate, the ladder and the notes; the loop also rebuilds it at the start of a soak when it is older than 24 h and after every kept patch.

HOW TO STOP AND RESTART

  • the switch: state/self/STOP; present now: no, the loop runs at its next tick. While it exists the tick refuses to start (exit 0, one line in the day's log) and a running soak ends between rounds.
  • the pid lock: state/self-code/autopilot.lock (one autopilot per tree); present now: no. A lock whose process is gone is taken over by the next run and the takeover is printed, so a crash never needs a hand to clear it.

Stop the loop, then start it again:

node -e "require('fs').writeFileSync('state/self/STOP', 'stopped by hand')"
node -e "require('fs').rmSync('state/self/STOP', {force: true})"

Take the tasks off the machine, or put them back (the same lines as above), or run the autopilot task once now:

node tools/schedule-autopilot.mjs --remove
node tools/schedule-autopilot.mjs --register
node tools/schedule-autopilot.mjs --run-now
node tools/schedule-ladder.mjs --remove
node tools/schedule-ladder.mjs --register
schtasks /delete /tn BrainAutopilot /f
schtasks /delete /tn BrainLadder /f
schtasks /run /tn BrainAutopilot

A soak that was killed continues from its checkpoint (state/self/soak-<runId>.json) with:

node bin/brain.mjs self-code --auto --resume

HOW THE UNDONE WORK GETS DONE WITHOUT CLAUDE

The loop is self/autopilot.mjs (run by the 05:00 task through bin/brain.mjs self-code --auto --soak 90). Each candidate passes five walls in order, ceiling, patch, evidence, gate, record, and stops at the first it fails; a kept patch is written to the real tree only after the whole gate is GREEN, and a red gate reverts it byte for byte. HOW TO DEPLOY THE SITE

node web/build.mjs
node tools/deploy.mjs web/dist

node web/build.mjs writes web/dist (the organism page, findings, portfolio, ladder and this file at /handoff). node tools/deploy.mjs web/dist runs the Vercel CLI through npx (npx vercel@latest), links the project "dilation" and deploys to production, aliased to dilation.dev; it prints every command before it runs it. The CLI login made once on this machine by device login lives in the CLI's own data folder under %APPDATA% (com.vercel.cli); present now: NO. This file never reads it and carries no credential. If the deploy prints that the CLI is not logged in, he runs the login himself:

npx vercel@latest login
